region.text: the Argolid around Mycenae, the type site

ledger.note: c. 1750 BCE: the Mycenaean age opens in the Argolid. Infobox 'c. 1750 - c. 1050 BC'; in the Early Mycenaean period (c. 1750-1400 BC) the shaft grave 'became the most common form of elite burial' and gave the period its name. The page gives the type site, not a boundary.

region.text: the mainland palatial world: 'Pylos, Tiryns, and Midea in the Peloponnese', 'Orchomenos, Thebes, and Athens in Central Greece', 'Iolcos in Thessaly'

ledger.note: c. 1500 BCE: Mycenaean centres cover the mainland from the Peloponnese to Thessaly. Cliopatria's first shape at its own date; the page names the centres but dates no consolidation ('Mycenaean civilization began around 1750 BC'; 'Palaces proper are datable from c. 1400 BC'; Helladic chronology page: LH IIA 1635-1470 BC). Re-read 2026-10-18: both pages silent on the extent, so the date stays at confidence 1.

region.text: the palace of Knossos and Crete

ledger.note: c. 1450 BCE: a Mycenaean elite takes Knossos and Crete. 'By c. 1450 BC, the palace of Knossos was ruled by a Mycenaean elite'; the page speaks of a 'mainland conquest of Crete c. 1450'; Knossos page: 'After about 1450 BC, Knossos became an important Mycenaean administrative centre.'

region.text: Miletos (Milawata in Hittite), 'Mycenaean Greece's main base in Asia Minor'

ledger.note: c. 1450 BCE: Mycenaeans settle Miletus. Excavations 'indicate the existence of a Mycenaean settlement there already from c. 1450 BC'; presence also reached Iasus and Ephesus. Cliopatria never draws Miletus; its Hittite row covers the Ionian coast from -1300.

region.text: 'several other Aegean islands, reaching as far as Rhodes'

ledger.note: c. 1400 BCE: Mycenaean colonists reach Rhodes and the islands. The page: 'Starting in the 15th century BC, the Mycenaeans began to spread their influence throughout the Aegean and Western Anatolia' and 'Mycenaeans also colonized several other Aegean islands, reaching as far as Rhodes'; History of Rhodes page: 'In the 15th century BC, Mycenaean Greeks settled.' The century is the pages', the year -1400 Cliopatria's (its -1400 shape adds Rhodes); the Ialysos page, opened for a date, is silent on Mycenaean settlement.

region.text: the Arzawa lands of western Anatolia around Millawanda

ledger.note: c. 1315 BCE: Ahhiyawa backs the Arzawa revolt against the Hittites. The page: c. 1315 BC 'an anti-Hittite rebellion headed by Arzawa, a Hittite vassal state, received support from Ahhiyawa'; Hittite records mention Ahhiyawa 'from c. 1400 to c. 1220 BC', first with 'the military activities of an Ahhiyawan warlord, Attarsiya' c. 1400. The zone is the coast around Miletus; the Hittite dossier (me-04) should carry the matching contest. Miletus page: 'In c. 1320 BC, the city supported an anti-Hittite rebellion of Uhha-Ziti of nearby Arzawa' and Muršili's generals attacked Millawanda and burned parts of it (the page ties the raid to that rebellion, with no separate date); the pages differ by five years, and -1315 is kept as the Mycenaean page's year.

region.text: 'Mycenaean settlements appeared in Epirus and Macedonia': the Macedonian coast, Lemnos, Aetolia-Acarnania and the Ionian islands

ledger.note: c. 1240 BCE: Mycenaean settlement reaches the Macedonian coast and the western seaboard. Cliopatria's date for its enlarged shape; the page's sentence is undated (re-read 2026-10-18: 'Mycenaean settlements also appeared in Epirus, Macedonia, on islands in the Aegean Sea', no date). The Troad (contest below) and Lesbos (separate gain below) are excluded.

region.text: Lesbos (Lazpa), where Piyama-Radu 'later invaded the island of Lesbos, which then passed into Ahhiyawan control'

ledger.note: c. 1240 BCE: Lesbos passes into Ahhiyawan control. Under Hattusili III (c. 1267-1237 BC) Piyama-Radu, supported by the king of Ahhiyawa, 'later invaded the island of Lesbos, which then passed into Ahhiyawan control'. The page gives no year inside the reign and names no state that held Lesbos before, so the counterpart is nobody (a Hittite dossier that records Lazpa as Hittite-held would need the matching loss); -1240 is Cliopatria's date for the Lesbos cells and falls at the end of the reign.

c. 1240 BCE: Ahhiyawan hostility reaches Wilusa. Under Hattusili III (c. 1267-1237 BC) Piyama-Radu's unrest 'may have extended to the region of Wilusa'; the Tawagalawa letter refers to 'an earlier Wilusa episode involving hostility on the part of Ahhiyawa' (Ahhiyawa page); the Milawata letter, dated 'around 1240 BC' (Milawata letter page), demands 'a pretender from Wilusa'. Cliopatria draws the Troad as Mycenaean from -1240; drawn here as contested, not possessed. Lesbos, named in the same sentence, 'passed into Ahhiyawan control' and is a gain (above).

region.text: the coast of western Anatolia around Miletus

ledger.note: c. 1220 BCE: the last Hittite record of Ahhiyawa in western Anatolia. 'In c. 1220 BC, the king of Ahhiyawa is again reported to have been involved in an anti-Hittite uprising in western Anatolia'; no treaty is recorded, a de facto end. The Tawagalawa letter had implied 'Miletus (Millawanda) was under his control' (Ahhiyawa page). Miletus page: the Milawata letter ('less securely dated'; c. 1240 BC, Tudhaliya IV, per the Milawata letter page) has the city 'now under Hittite control', yet Miletus was 'a Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor from c. 1450 to 1100 BC': the ground changed hands within the contest and ended Mycenaean, so no Hittite takeover is drawn after -1220. The Tudhaliya IV page gives the Sausgamuwa treaty's list of equals as 'the king of Assyria <and the king of Ahhiyawa>' (restored reading) and says nothing of a removal; no event.

c. 1220 BCE: the Wilusa contest ends with the last Hittite mention of Ahhiyawa; scholars suggest the mythic Trojan War 'could have a historical basis' in this era's turmoil. The Troad stays outside the Mycenaean shapes.

c. 1190 BCE: Mycenae burns a second time and Tiryns becomes the largest centre. Mycenae's second destruction 'in c. 1190 BC or shortly thereafter' ended its status as a major power; Tiryns 'became the largest local center during the post-palatial period'. Earlier: the first wave of destruction c. 1250 BC (Thebes burned); Tiryns's palace destroyed by earthquake 1200 BC; Pylos destroyed by fire c. 1180 BC (Late Bronze Age collapse page).

region.text: the Macedonian coast, Lemnos, Lesbos, the western seaboard and the Ionian islands, and three Cycladic cells

ledger.note: c. 1150 BCE: the outer Mycenaean settlements fall away in the post-palatial decades (26 cells: Macedonian coast 12, Lesbos 5, Lemnos and neighbours 3, Ionian islands 3, three Cycladic cells). Cliopatria's date for its shrunken shape; the pages date the palace destructions ('Up to 90% of small sites in the Peloponnese were abandoned') but not the end of the northern, western and island settlements; Lesbos, which 'passed into Ahhiyawan control' c. 1240, has no end date on the Mycenaean page. Miletus is not part of this loss: it stays Mycenaean until c. 1100 (next event).

region.text: Miletus, 'a Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor from c. 1450 to 1100 BC'

ledger.note: c. 1100 BCE: the Mycenaean stronghold at Miletus ends. Miletus page: 'Miletus was a Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor from c. 1450 to 1100 BC' and 'During the collapse of Bronze Age civilization, Miletus was burnt again, presumably by the Sea Peoples' (the burning is undated); Mycenaean Greece page: 'a sizable and prosperous Mycenaean center until the 12th century BC'. The Greek Dark Ages dossier does not draw Miletus until it adds Ionia (-1000), so the land goes to no state.

region.text: the post-palatial Greek world: mainland, Crete and the islands

ledger.note: c. 1100 BCE: the Mycenaean world passes into the Greek Dark Ages. The infobox ends the period 'c. 1050 BC' (LH IIIC Late 1100-1070/1040 BC) and the Greek Dark Ages page begins 'c. 1180'; Cliopatria's handover at -1100, the LH IIIC Middle/Late boundary, is kept. 'Mycenaean refugees migrated to Cyprus and the Levantine coast.' The 'Dorian invasion' is a hypothesis 'considered a myth by most scholars' (Dorian invasion page).

wars.name: Hittite-Ahhiyawa conflicts in western Anatolia

zones.text: Lazpa (Lesbos), invaded by Piyama-Radu and then 'passed into Ahhiyawan control'

wars.outcome: No border settled: the pages record Attarsiya's raids (c. 1400 BC), Ahhiyawan support for the Arzawa revolt (c. 1315, c. 1320 on the Miletus page), the 'Wilusa episode' and Piyama-Radu's raids on Wilusa and Lesbos under Hattusili III (c. 1267-1237), when 'The king of Ahhiyawa is recognized as a Great King', and a last anti-Hittite uprising c. 1220. Miletus remained the Mycenaean base (a stronghold c. 1450-1100 per the Miletus page, though the Milawata letter, c. 1240, has it 'under Hittite control'); Wilusa stayed outside Mycenaean possession; Lesbos 'then passed into Ahhiyawan control'.
wars.note: Intermittent, not a continuous war; the ledger's contests run -1315..-1220 (Miletus coast) and -1240..-1220 (Troad); Lesbos is a gain (-1240), not a contest. Attarsiya c. 1400 is a raid, not ground held. The Ahhiyawa page as fetched lacks the Milawata letter and the Sausgamuwa treaty; the repair opened the Miletus, Milawata letter and Tudhaliya IV pages: Muršili's generals burned parts of Millawanda (Miletus page, undated beyond the c. 1320 rebellion), the Milawata letter dates 'around 1240 BC' (Tudhaliya IV), and the treaty's list of equals reads 'the king of Assyria <and the king of Ahhiyawa>' (restored reading, no removal stated). The Hittite dossier (me-04) decides whether Miletus is drawn Hittite-held 1240-1220.

wars.name: Late Bronze Age collapse (Aegean destructions)
belligerents: unknown attackers (Sea Peoples, internal revolt or earthquake, per the pages)

zones.text: the Peloponnese, where 'Up to 90% of small sites' were abandoned

wars.outcome: Every palace destroyed: Mycenae 1250 (earthquake) and 1190 (fires), Tiryns 1200 (earthquake), Thebes sacked repeatedly between 1300 and 1200, Pylos c. 1180 (fire); 'none of the Mycenaean palaces of the Late Bronze Age survived', the Acropolis of Athens perhaps excepted. No land changed state; the outer settlements were abandoned by c. 1150.
wars.note: Not a war between states; listed because it moved the border at -1150 and ended the palatial state. The collapse 'coincides with the activity of the Sea Peoples', defeated by Ramesses III c. 1175 BC (Mycenaean page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders: every shape is an archaeological distribution of palatial centres and settlements, and the page says the Linear B texts 'are too fragmentary for the reconstruction of the political landscape'. The Anatolian coast and the north Aegean are the least certain; Crete after c. 1450 the best attested.

notes:
Written by the eu-01-a research agent on 2026-10-18 from five pages (budget: up to 5); repaired the same day after review with six more pages.

Start and end: the page dates the period c. 1750-1050 BC; Cliopatria's row runs -1500..-1101. The dossier starts at -1750 with a new Argolid-core keyframe and ends at -1100 (Cliopatria's handover, between the Mycenaean page's 1050 and the Dark Ages page's 1180); the Greek Dark Ages dossier starts -1100 to match.

Cliopatria corrections: Crete should join at -1450, not -1400 (new keyframe -1450); Miletus, the Mycenaean base in Asia Minor from c. 1450, is never drawn by Cliopatria and is added at 20 km to the -1450..-1200 shapes; the 'Turkey' part of the -1240..-1200 shapes is the Troad (Troy), not Miletus, and it is removed from the shapes and drawn as a contest with the Hittites (-1240..-1220) because the pages record hostility and raids, not possession. Lesbos stays in the shapes: the Mycenaean page says Piyama-Radu 'later invaded the island of Lesbos, which then passed into Ahhiyawan control', so it enters as a gain at -1240 (repair after review). Miletus stays to c. 1100 (Miletus page) and is lost at the dissolve. Cliopatria's Hittite row (-1300 on) reaches the Ionian coast but never overlaps the Mycenaean shapes.

Confidence-1 events: the -1500 mainland consolidation, the -1240 north and west, the -1150 withdrawal are Cliopatria's dates for undated page statements (re-read, still silent); the -1400 Rhodes settlement is dated to the 15th century by two pages (confidence 2).

Counterparts: hittites (me-04) should carry contest events for the Miletus coast -1315..-1220 and the Troad -1240..-1220; no Hittite loss of Lesbos is recorded (the Lesbos gain has counterpart nobody). States Cliopatria lacks that touch this dossier: Arzawa (western Anatolia, Hittite vassal/rebel), Wilusa (the Troad), Alashiya (Cyprus), and the Mycenaean palace states (Pylos, Thebes, Tiryns, Orchomenos) which the scope assigns to batch eu-01-x; the Knossos palace destruction c. 1350 is noted in the -1300 keyframe, not as a loss, since Crete stayed Mycenaean.

Gazetteer names lacking: Pylos, Tiryns, Argos, Argolid, Messenia, Laconia, Lesbos (Mitilini used), Lemnos; Thebes (Greece) and Mycenae exist. Pages not opened for want of budget: Wilusa, Pylos, Trojan War. Opened in the repair: Miletus, Milawata letter, Tudhaliya IV, Helladic chronology, History of Rhodes, Ialysos (silent). Cliopatria drops six cells of the -1300 shape at -1240 (three near Samos and Ikaria, 26.2-26.95 E 37.6-37.7 N, never regained; three Cycladic, regained at -1220 and dropped at -1150) with no page to explain them; left as Cliopatria draws them.
